tests.description: a valid PNG is saved in the upload folder
tests.input:
(lambda ns: (exec("import os, tempfile, types
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
blob = b'\x89PNG' + b'0' * 100
f = types.SimpleNamespace(filename='photo.png', content_type='image/png', read=lambda n=-1, _b=blob: _b if n < 0 else _b[:n])
try:
    p = save_upload(f, d)
    r = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(p)) == os.path.abspath(d) and open(p, 'rb').read() == blob
except ValueError:
    r = 'ValueError' if not os.listdir(d) else 'ValueError after writing'
", ns), ns['r'])[-1])(dict(globals()))

exercise.summary: save_upload(file, upload_dir) stores an uploaded file (file has .filename, .content_type and .read(n=-1)) but trusts everything the client sends. Fix it so that: the file always lands directly inside upload_dir, whatever the file name; only PNG and JPEG are accepted, checked against the file's first bytes (ALLOWED_TYPES maps each type to its signature), not just content_type; and files larger than MAX_BYTES are rejected. A rejected upload raises ValueError and writes nothing.
